introduction: Hawaiʻi General Assistance is a temporary cash program for certain adults with a disabling condition and little or no income. DHS uses a medical assessment as well as financial eligibility checks.

sections.who: The state describes adults aged 18–64 without minor dependents who are temporarily disabled, do not qualify for Social Security and do not qualify under a federal assistance category. A DHS medical board must certify inability to undertake substantial employment of at least 30 hours weekly for at least 60 days. Asset rules also apply.
sections.get: GA helps with essentials such as food, clothing and shelter. State funding is limited, and the benefit amount can change during the year.
sections.docs:
• Prepare income, asset and household information.
  • Have available medical records and the treating provider’s contact details.
  • Ask DHS what medical certification forms and identity records are needed for your case.
sections.apply:
1. Ask about a financial-assistance application

    Use the DHS BESSD contact route or call 1-855-643-1643. State clearly that you are asking about General Assistance.

  2. Explain the disability and household

    Describe the condition, work limitations and whether any minor dependents live with you.

  3. Complete the agency’s medical review

    Provide the requested records and follow the instructions for the DHS medical-board assessment.
sections.after: Keep benefit notices and respond to medical or financial review requests. Ask DHS about a different assistance category if your household or disability circumstances change.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Hawaiʻi GA eligibility overview, BESSD contact and program information. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Is having no job enough to qualify?
No. GA has disability, age, household and financial requirements, including DHS medical certification.
Yes. DHS says the program’s annual funding can require benefit adjustments.
Is GA intended for families with minor children?
The published GA category is for adults without minor dependents. Ask DHS about the appropriate family program.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
